title: Twenty-Four Years of Empirical Research on Trust in AI: A Bibliometric Review of Trends, Overlooked Issues, and Future Directions
extended_summary:
This paper reviews over two decades of empirical research on trust in AI. The authors ask how trust in AI has been studied across disciplines, what publication and citation patterns characterize the field, and what conceptual or methodological gaps remain. Their motivation is to map a fragmented literature and identify overlooked issues in how trust is defined, measured, and interpreted.

The study uses a mixed-method review approach combining bibliometric analysis with qualitative content analysis. The corpus includes 1,156 core empirical articles and 36,306 cited articles published from 2000 to 2023, drawn from Scopus, Web of Science, ACM Library, PubMed, and IEEE Explorer. The paper does not study a single educational intervention or user population; instead, it surveys trust research across domains such as human-robot interaction, computer science, healthcare, transportation, and consumer AI. The analysis highlights publication trends, co-citation structures, keyword clusters, and the most influential theoretical works.

The main conclusions are that trust in AI research is dominated by Western/global-North and technical perspectives, with heavy reliance on exploratory methods and limited theoretical grounding. The literature heavily draws on foundational work in trust in automation, especially calibration, reliance, and appropriate use. The authors argue that more contextualized, inclusive, and theory-driven research is needed, along with stronger methodological rigor and attention to long-term, real-world human-AI interactions.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a bibliometric and qualitative review of prior trust-in-AI studies, not an empirical evaluation of an educational intervention. It does not present a clear experimental, quasi-experimental, or correlational study of outcomes in learners or teachers.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct measured educational impact; it synthesizes the research field on trust in AI and offers methodological recommendations. Any relevance to teacher-facing generative AI is indirect and conceptual rather than evidence of impact.
